description: The foreign parts are chosen over the whole derivation, and a %foreign constituent that the choice leaves out is ordinary, even when a token is emitted over it (engine §11). The first `inner` lies inside the foreign part `outer`, whose rule has no emission clause. So the walk reaches it and its own emission runs. The second lies inside the foreign part `held`, whose capture item emits a token over it. Each token has the source of its input token and sounds `b`, not `?`. `skipped` lies inside `gone`, which emits ε, so the walk does not reach it, and it emits nothing. It is no foreign part, so it takes in no text, and `tail`, the next foreign part, takes the space before it.
grammar:
%rule text outer held gone tail
%rule outer A inner
%foreign
%rule held $i(inner)
%emits $i <J>
%foreign
%rule inner B
%emits $ <I>
%foreign
%rule gone skipped
%emits ε
%rule skipped C
%emits $ <S>
%foreign
%rule tail D
%emits $ <T>
%foreign
